rows.core: Kraum and Tevesh partner stax leverages two commanders plus artifact mana to break parity under mana denial, Orb effects and Contamination while closing with Helm/void or Breach.
rows.positive: The Enigma Jewel is a low-cost artifact that may survive some stax filters and support activations of Helm of Obedience or other artifact abilities under a mana-denial lock.
rows.cut_cost: Mox Amber is a zero-cost accelerator whose colors can be enabled by either Kraum or Tevesh; it improves early lock deployment without adding a taxed activation payment.
rules: Kraum and Tevesh are separate legal partner commanders occupying two command slots within the same 100-card Commander deck.
Mox Amber can tap for a color among your controlled legendary creatures/planeswalkers; Tevesh provides black and Kraum blue/red.
The Enigma Jewel enters tapped and its mana can pay only costs of activated abilities, not spells or Tevesh's loyalty activation costs.
Under stax constraints, delayed access to activated-ability mana is not equivalent to a zero-mana artifact producing early spell mana.
Helm of Obedience has an activated ability costing mana; a Jewel contribution only matters if all colored/generic payments and library replacement interactions are legal.
rows.adverse: The swap risks weakening mana under Winter Orb and Contamination in exchange for a restricted tapped mana source that cannot cast lock pieces.
rows.followup: Record turn-one to turn-four lock deployment with/without Amber and actual Helm activation payments through active stax pieces.
rows.add: The Enigma Jewel // Locus of Enlightenment

rows.core: Crosis needs combat damage and {2}{B} to empty a targeted color of a player's hand, with Painter turning a chosen color into near-total hand disruption; discard payoffs convert hits to resources.
rows.positive: Relic of Sauron produces three Grixis-colored mana at once on tap, potentially funding Crosis's optional trigger and follow-up discard payoff spells in the long game.
rows.cut_cost: Black Market Connections repeatedly generates cards, Treasure and bodies (with life costs), supplying evasive combat protection and post-hit gas; losing it makes the hand-disruption engine brittle.
rules: Crosis triggers when dealing combat damage to a player; paying {2}{B} chooses a color and discards matching cards in that opponent's hand.
Painter's Servant applies its chosen color to all cards in hand as well as permanents, enabling broad Crosis discard if legal color targets remain.
Relic of Sauron costs four mana and taps for UBR, but its colored mana can't pay the whole {2}{B} cost without an additional two generic mana.
Black Market Connections offers per-turn draw, Treasure and changeling creature for life during precombat main, not just one-time mana.
A Crosis hit and a Relic activation compete with the actual timing of equipping/protecting a six-mana flyer.
rows.adverse: Higher-cost rock replacing a flexible draw/Treasure/fodder engine loses midgame resiliency; it doesn't help Crosis connect or change opponents' colors.
rows.followup: Count real protected Crosis combat connections and cards sustained with Connections versus Relic's additional colored mana; isolate Painter interaction.

rows.core: Davros requires each opponent to have lost at least three life during your turn for full end-step Dalek/token and villainous-choice value, amplified by copying choice triggers.
rows.positive: Darkwater Catacombs filters existing mana into both blue and black, which can aid reactive draw-or-discard and Dalek protection spells when mana-base colors are awkward.
rows.cut_cost: Geier Reach Sanitarium is a utility land that lets each player draw/discard, feeding discard-punishment payoffs and end-step resource pressure around Davros's Villainous Choice.
rules: Davros checks the 3-life threshold separately for each opponent during the turn, not whether they have discarded cards.
Darkwater Catacombs filters another paid mana into {U}{B}; it does not directly produce mana alone from a single untapped land without input.
Geier Reach Sanitarium has a colorless mana ability plus a paid group loot activation, allowing discard-payoff interaction in either turn's timing.
Geier Reach looting does not itself count as opponent life loss unless a card like Liliana's Caress or another payoff produces that loss.
Replacing a colorless utility land with colored filtering may improve castability but cannot be credited as an additional Davros trigger.
rows.adverse: The swap removes the unique repeatable discard activator, reducing sources that pressure Davros choice branches and enemy hands, for mana filtering that must have additional input.
rows.followup: Run source-paid Davros threshold and real multiplayer discard-damage sequences for Sanitarium versus Catacombs across color-disrupted starts.

rows.core: Edward converts tapped attacking/crewing Assassins, Pirates and Vehicles into end-step Treasures and awards playable exiled cards after Vehicles hit players.
rows.positive: Deadly Dispute can cash in a Treasure or expendable token to draw two cards and replace it with another Treasure, helping turn abundant Edward artifacts into cards.
rows.cut_cost: Jeska's Will offers burst red mana and exiled castable resources at three mana, frequently both effects when Edward is controlled and useful to deploy Vehicles or protected attack triggers.
rules: Deadly Dispute is an instant and additionally requires sacrificing an artifact or creature as part of casting cost.
Its Treasure production offsets one sacrificed artifact, but not its two mana expenditure or sacrificed Vehicle if used as fodder.
Edward checks relevant tapped Assassins, Pirates and Vehicles at his end-step trigger; sacrificing one before that check can lower the Treasure count.
Jeska's Will modes depend on targeted opponent hand count or top exiled cards, with both modes selectable if its caster controls a commander.
Edward's Vehicle-combat exiled play permission has its own timing and cannot be assumed to be duplicated by Dispute's draw.
rows.adverse: A conditional card draw exchange of two mana can lose development over Will's simultaneous burst and impulse cards; early Treasure count is not infinite.
rows.followup: Compare Edward end-step tapped counts and available Vehicles under a Dispute-sacrifice decision versus Jeska's Will with commander controlled.

rows.core: Any creature entering under your control this turn that hits a player in combat triggers 5/5 Dragon production; dash, ninjutsu and hasty threats spread connections.
rows.positive: Izzet Signet is stable two-mana filtering ramp, which can accelerate commander and later dash/ninjutsu costs if the color sources work out.
rows.cut_cost: Ragavan can attack quickly through dash, steal opposing exiled cards and generate Treasures after combat damage, simultaneously fueling first-entry attacks and colors.
rules: Goro-Goro and Satoru checks combat damage by a creature that entered the battlefield this turn, not merely any hasty creature.
Ragavan's dash casts it for an alternate cost and gives haste, so a newly entered Ragavan can qualify after dealing combat damage.
Ragavan's combat trigger makes a Treasure and exiles an opponent's top card for possible casting, creating immediate attacker-specific resources.
Izzet Signet itself cannot attack or deal combat damage and its filtered mana requires an additional source/input to activate.
Cutting a qualifying first-turn combat attacker can lower Dragon token production even if the replacement improves abstract ramp count.
rows.adverse: Two-mana Signet cannot replace Ragavan's fresh combat trigger and the commander-specific route to Dragon generation; own ceiling is creature tempo.
rows.followup: Replay T2–T5 entrant combat damage, Dragon counts, and treasure tempo with actual evasive Dash availability and Signet starts.

rows.core: A 10-power commander seeks haste/evasion and infect or double strike while avoiding its huge entry drawback; Torpor Orb, Stifle and Dress Down suppress liability.
rows.positive: Tribute Mage can search the deck for a mana-value-2 artifact (including Torpor Orb when in library), making one specific drawback-suppression piece more accessible.
rows.cut_cost: Vampiric Tutor is one-black instant-speed universal top-of-library tutor that can find whatever missing protection, infect kill, haste source or Torpor Orb the current state needs.
rules: Lord of Tresserhorn's enters trigger forces two creatures sacrificed, two opponent cards drawn, and life payments unless suppressed/handled.
Tribute Mage enters and searches only an artifact card of mana value exactly two, far narrower than Vampiric Tutor.
Torpor Orb prevents creature enter-the-battlefield triggers, including Lord's, only if already on battlefield before it would trigger.
Vampiric Tutor puts any searched card on top and costs 2 life rather than putting it directly in hand.
Tutoring Torpor Orb without verifying the timing and Lord survival is not equivalent to eliminating the enter trigger.
rows.adverse: Three-mana specific tutor replaces the most flexible low-cost safety valve for both entry suppression and infect-kill packages; extra creature body is rarely the Voltron payoff.
rows.followup: Compare actual arrival-with-protection turns and tutor accessible kill windows, including whether Tribute Mage gets Torpor Orb in time.
